clue.text: Formal caution suggested by this court

blocks.note: starch is stiff formality of manner
the amber traffic light warns drivers to take care

explanation.surface: A stern official warning, as might be handed down by some tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: The STAR CHAMBER was an English court of Tudor and Stuart times, notorious for arbitrary judgments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was a historic English tribunal sitting at Westminster, so it is a court.

clue.text: Protection across the board? It may help one sleep at night

definitions.text: It may help one sleep at night

blocks.note: first meaning: complete cover against every risk

blocks.clueFragment: It may help one sleep at night
blocks.note: second meaning: a child's comfort blanket

explanation.surface: Total insurance cover that lets a worrier rest easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of a blanket spread right across everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both all-round reassurance and the cherished blanket a small child clings to at bedtime.

clue.text: Yale elmy? That could be nonsense

indicators.note: 'could be' says the jumble may become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: a meaningless pair of words taken as letters

explanation.surface: Someone stares at the gibberish 'Yale elmy' and dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is openly nonsense, which fits the answer's meaning: ALL MY EYE is an old British phrase for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All my eye' is a dated British idiom for humbug or claptrap, so it means nonsense.

clue.text: About to be included in Conservative party's statement of belief

indicators.note: something included in goes inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
re means about, concerning
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party's manifesto is about to be adopted by the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative party' reads as one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces either side of the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a formal set of principles a person or group holds.

clue.text: Metal bracket in corner by press

indicators.note: 'by' means next to, so one part sits beside the other

blocks.note: an angle is a corner
to iron is to press clothes

explanation.surface: A workshop scene: a metal bracket fixed in the corner next to a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests a cupboard or a newspaper; here it is the verb for smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Angle iron is L-section steel used to make brackets and frames.

clue.text: Game bird, initially with crest

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter only

blocks.note: first letter of bird
a crest is the ridge of a hill

explanation.surface: A game bird is described, at first glance, as having a crest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.

clue.text: What Carter once did successfully, but not his predecessor?

definitions.text: What Carter once did successfully, but not his predecessor?

blocks.note: surface reading: a feat Jimmy Carter achieved
setter's reading: Gerald Ford also stood in 1976 and lost to Carter

explanation.walkthrough: Carter won the 1976 US election against the sitting president Gerald Ford, who had never won a presidential race; both campaigned, only one succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Running for office is campaigning for it, and Carter's 1976 campaign won the White House.

clue.text: Mean scoundrel after drink for pet

indicators.note: 'after' places the first-named part later in the word

blocks.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
dog is an old word for a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A nasty rogue, after a drink, goes looking for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered pet dog, kept to sit on its owner's knee.

clue.text: Handsome youth a lecturer is after

blocks.note: taken as written
a don is a university lecturer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man is being pursued by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as part of the wordplay but simply means 'sought by' in the surface; the letters run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, and his name now stands for any very attractive young man.

clue.text: Spanish mayor called a lunatic

indicators.note: a lunatic is crazed, so the letters are jumbled madly

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has called the Spanish mayor a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcalde is the Spanish title for the head of a town council, a mayor or magistrate.

clue.text: Smiled broadly having good cooked dinner

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone beamed happily over a good home-cooked meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin is to smile widely, so the past tense matches smiled broadly.

clue.text: Match between local teams in English city

blocks.note: first meaning: a game between neighbouring rivals
second meaning: a city in the East Midlands

explanation.surface: A local rivalry fixture being played in some English city.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a local derby is a game between two clubs from the same area.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fixture between neighbouring rival clubs and the East Midlands city.

clue.text: Governor worried about wicket covered with weeds

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and pulled about, so its letters are mixed
'about' means going around, so the jumble surrounds what follows

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A groundsman-like governor frets that the cricket pitch has gone to seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Overgrown describes ground choked with uncontrolled plants, so covered with weeds fits.

clue.text: Scoff, upset by famous industrialist's film

indicators.note: 'by' means beside, so one part goes next to the other
upset in a down-the-page sense means turned over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: J. Paul Getty was a famous American oil magnate
scoff is British slang for food, as is grub

explanation.surface: Someone sneers, put out by a famous tycoon's movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like a verb, to mock; here it is the British noun for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gettysburg is a 1993 American Civil War film about the battle of that name.

clue.text: Bairn, surprisingly, was hard to indoctrinate

indicators.note: 'surprisingly' says the word turns out in an unexpected form, so rearrange it

blocks.note: a bairn is a Scottish word for child; taken as letters
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Scottish child surprisingly proved hard to indoctrinate.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash someone is to force beliefs on them, which is to indoctrinate.

clue.text: Love quiet American work

blocks.note: love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O
p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Praise for a gentle American piece of art.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic composition, a creative work.

clue.text: Frosty spell may cause viral infection to flare up

blocks.note: the common cold is caused by a virus
to snap is to lose one's temper suddenly

explanation.surface: A bout of freezing weather can make a virus flare up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' suggests magic; here it is a period of weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold snap is a short sudden period of very low temperatures.

clue.text: Girl in public school, losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter is dropped

blocks.note: Rugby is a famous English public (private fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A girl at a boarding school grows downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an old private boarding school, such as Rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's given name, as crosswords often define names by sex alone.

clue.text: Suspension of business in bay

blocks.note: first meaning: a break in a parliament's or court's sittings
second meaning: an alcove or niche in a wall

explanation.surface: Trading halted in a harbour bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an adjournment of proceedings and an indented alcove set back in a wall.

clue.text: Most uncommon to receive gen in jungle

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: rarest means least common
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An explorer gets rare intelligence while deep in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, from 'general information'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainforest is dense tropical woodland, which is what a jungle is.

clue.text: Special gift adult left in shelter

indicators.note: 'in' places the first parts inside the shelter word

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
L is the abbreviation for left
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A present for a grown-up has been left in a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude, an innate ability given to someone.

clue.text: Girl is excellent right away

indicators.note: 'away' says that letter is sent off and removed

blocks.note: stellar means outstanding
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A girl is brilliant straight off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'at once'; the two words split into an abbreviation and the instruction to remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's given name, Latin for star.

clue.text: Admonished, head of council went quickly

indicators.note: the head of something is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of council
hastened means hurried

explanation.surface: The council leader was rebuked and hurried away.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to rebuke or correct someone, so the past tense fits admonished.

clue.text: Extremely debatable, my colour scheme

indicators.note: at the extremes means only the very ends of the word are taken

blocks.note: the end letters of debatable
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: Someone frets that their colour choices are highly questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the furnishing and colour arrangement of a room, its overall colour scheme.

clue.text: Exercise may make doctor unwell!

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A wry warning that working out could make even a medic sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated training routine, a form of exercise or practice.

clue.text: Variety of kilts, notice, back in Hebridean archipelago

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are rearranged
'back' says the word is read in the backwards direction

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A display of kilts is announced back in the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: ST KILDA is a remote island group west of the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: St Kilda is an isolated group of islands in the Hebrides, abandoned by its people in 1930.

clue.text: Business interest

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm or company
second meaning: something that matters to one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a commercial stake, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commercial firm and a matter of relevance or worry to someone.

clue.text: Favourite in form? Note odds in the race fluctuating

indicators.note: something fluctuating keeps shifting, so the words are rearranged
'in' puts the preceding piece inside the rearranged words

blocks.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written before rearranging
SP is starting price, the odds on a horse when a race begins

explanation.surface: A racing tip for the form favourite, with odds shifting before the off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' suggests a horse's racing form; here it is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's pet is the pupil a teacher favours, and a form is a school class.
